LESSON: DECIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.5: Decimals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Decimals, part of Numbers in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How can you use decimals in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify decimals up to ten thousandths in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Decimals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. round off decimals up to 3 decimal places in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Decimals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. convert decimals to fractions and fractions to decimals in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Decimals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. convert decimals to percentages and percentages to decimals in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Decimals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. add decimals up to 4- decimal places in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Decimals in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. subtract decimals up to 4-decimal places in different situations, ● Learners with low vision to be guided to calculate place value of decimals up to ten thousandths using place value apparatus in appropriate font and colour contrast. Learners with blindness be guided to use place value setters with tactile marks to calculate the place value of decimals up to ten thousandths. ● In pairs, learners to be guided to relate place value of decimals up to ten thousandths to the number of decimal places. ● Learners to be guided to round off decimals up to 3 decimal places. ● Learners with low vision to be guided to change decimals to fractions using a square or rectangular grid in appropriate How can you use decimals in real life? 15

   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Decimals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: The learner develops self-drive when carrying out addition and subtraction on decimals using various

learning resources.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner displays determination when converting decimals to percentages and percentages to

decimal.

PCIs:

• Safety and security: The learner safely uses the digital devices with assistive technology to play games on decimals

observing cyber safety and security rules.

Links to other Learning Areas:
• Science and Technology: The learner uses weighing machines when measuring the masses of different substances in

decimals during practicals.

17

• Agriculture and Nutrition: The learner uses weighing machines when measuring cooking ingredients in decimals.
